name: mcp__html__html_find
description: Finds elements in an HTML file by `text` (literal visible text, case-sensitive; the deepest matches, at most 20, with their ancestors as outline lines) or by `id` (the element and its child elements). Each element shows its @n ref and all its attributes. Ends with the match count and the file hash.

file.description: Optional when the folder has one .html or .htm file

name: mcp__html__html_change
description: Changes one element of an HTML file and saves it; all other bytes stay the same. Name the element by `ref` and `hash`; or by `text` (the deepest element whose visible text contains it; with `tag`, the innermost of that tag); or by `id`, with `child` and `n` for its n-th child of that tag. If the name fits several elements, nothing changes and the matches are listed. Operations: remove; replace (`html`); insert_after (`html`); set_attribute (`attribute`, `value`); replace_text (`old` is visible text in one text node, with entities decoded and whitespace runs as one space; `new` replaces it). `value` and `new` are plain text. Not for html, head or body. When the task quotes visible text inside the element, call html_change with that `text`, and with `tag` when the task names the element's tag; html_find is not needed first.

name: mcp__html__html_outline
description: The reading view of an HTML file: one element per line with its @n ref, indented by depth; text as "| text" lines. Scripts, styles, comments, SVG content, hidden content and most attributes are left out. Pages of up to 20,000 tokens, with the file hash. Use html_find when you know some text or an id.
